content.title: About
content.content: White sugar is obtained from sugarcane or sugar beet through extraction, purification, crystallization and drying. It consists of fine crystals that dissolve easily in water and is widely used in cooking, baking and the food industry.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sugar was known in ancient Mesopotamia and Egypt.
The first industrial process for producing beet sugar was developed in the early 19th century.
White sugar is almost pure sucrose – a disaccharide of glucose and fructose.
Sugar acts as a preservative because it slows microbial growth by creating osmotic pressure.
In baking, sugar not only sweetens but also influences texture, color and structure.

items.title: Quick source of energy
items.content: Sucrose is rapidly absorbed, providing an immediate boost of glucose to the bloodstream.

items.title: Supports hydration during intense exercise
items.content: Sugar in sports drinks helps replenish glycogen stores and maintain fluid balance.

items.title: Improves taste and appetite
items.content: A modest amount of sugar can stimulate appetite and enhance flavor, which can be helpful in cases of undernutrition.

items.title: Blood sugar spikes
items.content: Excessive sugar intake can cause hyperglycemia and contribute to the development of type 2 diabetes.

items.title: Dental caries risk
items.content: Sugar feeds oral bacteria, promoting plaque formation and tooth decay.

items.title: Empty calories
items.content: Sugar provides 4 kcal/g without essential nutrients, so overconsumption can lead to weight gain.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Although rare, some individuals may react to processing additives used in refined sugar.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Sugar is added to tea, coffee, baked goods, desserts, sauces and marinades. It can be used for caramelization, making syrups, sprinkling on fruit, and as a preservative in jams.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store sugar in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from moisture and strong odors. Properly stored, it remains stable for years.
